2 وَكّب , inf. n. تَوْكِيبٌ, [app., He pursued a middle or just, way with respect to the صِرَار; which is a cord, or a piece of rag, that is bound over a she-camel's udder, or teats, to prevent her young one from sucking her]. (K: the inf. n. is explained by the words المُقَارَبَةُ فِى الصِّرَارِ: written in the TA الصرأر; to which is there added, with kesr.) ―
-b2- See 1.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
